chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isma'il al-Ja'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Possessors of Steadfastness among the Prophets are five: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad (peace be upon them all).
ai.seo_question: Who are the five Ulul 'Azm prophets in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* explicitly lists Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad as the five *Ulul 'Ulul 'Azm* (Possessors of Steadfastness), a designation highlighting their unique endurance in establishing divine law. In Shia scholarship, this chain of transmission (*isnad*) underscores the continuity of prophetic mission, linking the foundational patriarchs to the Seal of the Prophets, while the chapter title emphasizes their role as owners of distinct *Shari'a* (divine legislation).
